```cpp
DataStreamPtr Archive::createFromFile(const String& fileName)
{

                "This archive does not support creation of files.", 
                "Archive::createFromFile");
}
```

Please note that this is a simple correction and the actual solution may vary depending on the rest of the codebase and the specific requirements of the project.

                  sweepFiring(false), damageAllies(false) {}
raw:
The clang-tidy `cppcoreguidelines-prefer-member-initializer` is a warning about the use of member initializer lists. In this case, the member variables `sweepInitDst`, `sweepGoalDst`, `sweepCurrDst`, `sweepStartAngle`, `sweepFiring`, and `damageAllies` are all assigned the same value in the constructor, which is not a good practice.

Here is the corrected version of the function:

```cpp
SweepFireState() : sweepInitDst(0.0f), sweepGoalDst(0.0f), sweepCurrDst(0.0f), sweepStartAngle(0.0f),
                  sweepFiring(false), damageAllies(false) {}
```

In the corrected version, each member variable is assigned a value in its own member initializer list. This is a better practice as it clearly shows the purpose of each variable.

raw:
The `modernize-pass-by-value` finding in Clang-Tidy is about avoiding unnecessary copies of objects. In this case, the `IActionExecutor` class is a simple constructor that takes a `std::string` by value, which is a good practice.

Here is the corrected version of the code:

```cpp
IActionExecutor(const std::string& command,
		const std::string& description, bool cheatRequired = false)
	: command(command)
	, description(description)
	, cheatRequired(cheatRequired)
{}
```

In this version, the `IActionExecutor` class is a simple constructor that takes `command`, `description`, and `cheatRequired` by value. This is a more efficient way to pass these arguments to the constructor, as it avoids unnecessary copies.

```cpp
static bool is_lock_free()

		details::static_is_lock_free<std::uint32_t>::value == 2 &&

		details::static_is_lock_free<typename details::thread_id_converter<details::thread_id_t>::thread_id_numeric_size_t>::value == 2;
}
```

So, the function is not redundant.

The function `rawOffsetPointer` is a template function that takes a pointer to a type `T` and an offset of type `ptrdiff_t`. It returns a pointer to a type `T`.

The function is using redundant parentheses to cast the pointer to `(const char*)`. This is not necessary and can be removed to simplify the code.

Here is the corrected function:

```cpp
template <class T>
static OGRE_FORCE_INLINE const T* rawOffsetPointer(const T* ptr, ptrdiff_t offset)
{
    return (const T*)(ptr + offset);
}
```

This function now correctly returns a pointer to a type `T` by adding the offset to the pointer.

raw:
The `modernize-pass-by-value` finding in Clang-Tidy is about unnecessary copying of objects. In this case, the `UDPConnection` class is receiving a `std::shared_ptr<ip::udp::socket>` and a `const ip::udp::endpoint&`, and these are passed by value. This is not necessary because the `std::shared_ptr` and `ip::udp::endpoint` are reference types, not value types. Therefore, the `UDPConnection` class can pass these by reference.

Here is the corrected code:

```cpp
UDPConnection::UDPConnection(const std::shared_ptr<ip::udp::socket>& netSocket, const ip::udp::endpoint& myAddr)
	: addr(myAddr)
	, sharedSocket(true)
	, mySocket(netSocket)
{
	Init();
}
```

In this corrected version, the `UDPConnection` class is receiving `std::shared_ptr<ip::udp::socket>` and `const ip::udp::endpoint&` by reference, not by value.
